newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end higher, Samsung leads late buying.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end higher, Samsung leads late buying.

text.p: The South Korean stock market rose on Tuesday, led by buying in blue chips, brokers said.

The improving sentiment was given an added boost when Samsung Electronics did an about-face in the afternoon session on reports the U.S. semiconductor industry's August book-to-bill ratio was expected to improve against July.
The composite stock index rose 5.66 points to a provisional close of 803.04. Despite the index climb, declining shares beat advancers 444 to 407.
This was the first time the index has ended above the 800 point resistance line since August 19.
"Most blue chips and high-tech shares followed Samsung higher," said a Jardine Fleming broker. "Institutional investors were active buyers."

The U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association will release its book-to-bill report on Tuesday. U.S. analysts said they were expecting the ratio to be between 0.86 and 0.92, against 0.85 in July. A South Korean paper, the Naewae Economic Daily, reported that the ratio was expected to be 0.88. Book-to-bill measures new orders for computer chips against shipments.
LG Electronics shares also soared, climbing 800 won to their upper limit of 14,800.

Brokers said sentiment on the market has brightened because the liquidity crunch was easing on falling interest rates, buying by newly established investment trusts and the goverment's supply of funds ahead of the Korean Thanksgiving holidays in late September. The prospects of an employee stock savings plan and more buying by foreign investors next month also boosted the mood.
But margin loans at securities houses continue to outstrip customer deposits, at 2.68 trillion won versus 2.39 trillion.
